subject: physics
label: Projectile Motion & Relative Velocity
blurb: A preview topic showing how the same trick-first format carries over to Physics — four sample problems, not yet a full verified bank.

toolkit.title: Switch to the relative frame first
toolkit.desc: For “when/where do A and B meet” problems, work in the frame of one object: \(\vec v_{AB}=\vec v_A-\vec v_B\). The problem usually collapses to 1-D in that frame.

toolkit.title: Resolve along the constraint, not default x–y
toolkit.desc: Pick axes along the incline, the string, or the wall — whichever direction has zero acceleration or zero velocity component — before writing any equation.

toolkit.title: Range/height/time are independent sub-problems
toolkit.desc: In projectile motion, vertical motion fixes time of flight; horizontal motion (constant velocity) then fixes range. Solve the vertical equation first, always.

toolkit.title: Symmetry before computation
toolkit.desc: Before setting up an integral or force balance, ask what symmetry (mirror, rotational) the configuration has — it often kills half the terms for free.

toolkit.title: Sanity-check with limiting cases
toolkit.desc: Plug in an extreme or special value (angle \(\to0\) or \(90^\circ\), mass ratio \(\to0\) or \(\infty\)) and check the formula matches the physically obvious answer.

toolkit.title: Constraint relations by differentiating geometry
toolkit.desc: When two motions are linked by a string/rod/incline, write the geometric length relation first, then differentiate it — don't guess the velocity relation directly.
